gaps.sentence: Every time I visit, she ___ something delicious from the garden.
gaps.hint: every time marks a repeated habit
gaps.explanation: 'Every time' marks a repeated action, which takes the present simple: brings.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.

gaps.sentence: What ___ at eleven o'clock last night? I called you twice.
gaps.hint: at eleven o'clock means a point in past
gaps.explanation: A specific past moment asks about an action in progress then, so the past continuous fits: were you doing.

gaps.sentence: They ___ married in a small ceremony in 2011.
gaps.explanation: A dated single event takes the past simple: got.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: I ___ what the problem is, so let me explain it to the others.
gaps.hint: see meaning understand is a state
gaps.explanation: When 'see' means 'understand', it is a state verb and cannot be continuous: see.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.
